exposure: routine umbilical cord blood gas analysis
selective umbilical cord blood gas analysis
Apgar score of less than seven at one minute
outcome: Risk of missing umbilical cord blood gas samples
cohort: 155,235 live singleton infants born in Sweden between 2008 and 2014
finding: Compared to routine sampling, selective umbilical cord blood gas sampling significantly increased the risks of missing samples in high-risk deliveries and in infants with birth asphyxia.
